Accessibility
Together we learn and grow
Where children grow alongside a whole village.
We are a small primary school in Somerset, working together as children, parents, staff, governors and the local community of Wookey, so that every child can thrive.
Warm, ambitious and rooted in community
Pick a doorway into the school — from our vision and curriculum to preschool life at Little Acorns.
OPAL - Outdoor Play and Learning
Our school believes that all children need opportunities to play that allow them to explore, manipulate, experience and affect their environment. Our children experience adventurous outdoor play every day through our commitment to OPAL play strategies and principles.
The Beehive
The Beehive: Nurture & Inclusive Provision at Wookey At Wookey Primary School, we are proud to be a fully inclusive setting. We believe that inclusion is not simply physical presence in a room, it is about a genuine sense of belonging. The Beehive is our small-group nurture setting designed to build safety, secure strong learning foundations, and ensure no child leaves Wookey without the skills to thrive.
Wellbeing
We prioritise wellbeing for our whole school community. We run a Wellbeing Action Group made up of children, staff, governors and parents to ensure we meet the needs of as many members of our community as possible.
Learning
Explore curriculum, the school day, safeguarding, results, e-safety, clubs and school funding information.
Welcome from the head
A village school with a big heart
By supporting and listening to each other, we learn to raise standards and expectations, ensuring that children leave our school as ambitious, independent, resilient and kind young people.
Please enjoy looking around our website, then make an appointment to come and meet us — to see the team in action and feel the warmth of school life.

Accessibility
Vision, Ethos and Values
Wookey Primary School's vision is rooted in engagement, independence, respect and resilience.
Wookey Primary School: Together we learn and grow
Our Vision
It is our view that success as a school is achieved only through engagement of all stakeholders: children, staff, parents and governors.
Our vision is to develop resilient, confident and emotionally intelligent children who demonstrate a love for learning that enables them to be active citizens who achieve all they want to in life.
We want our children to thrive academically, mentally and physically in a nurturing environment.
Our Ethos
Our Values
We will achieve our vision through a focus on our core values of engagement, independence, respect and resilience.
Our school curriculum has our values at the centre of it. Our values are woven throughout teaching, planning and communication.
Engagement: children build relationships, ask questions, generate ideas, try alternatives, plan and research, are curious and love learning.
Independence: children evaluate strengths, have pride in their learning, are organised, creative, show initiative and take responsibility.
Respect: children understand consequences, are mindful of others’ feelings, collaborate, listen, respect difference and value views that may differ from their own.
Resilience: children persevere, problem-solve, invite feedback, deal positively with praise and setbacks, manage emotions and show confidence.
British Values
Alongside and complementing our school values, sit the nationally-agreed British values. The Department for Education defines British values as having 5 different elements:
We use our weekly PSHE assemblies and our classroom discussions to teach and embed these values across subjects and experiences. Our children are also taught about protected characteristics and how to treat everyone with respect, no matter their differences, or similarity to each other. We give the children as many practical experiences as we can to help them put these values into practice and into context, as well as choosing curriculum and assembly books which represent the values, protected characteristics and stories from beyond their usual sphere of experience to trigger debate and encourage the children to consider and question.

About Us
Find out about Wookey Primary School, our values, admissions, staff, policies, wrap around care, inspection reports and vacancies.
Wookey Primary School is a village community school run by Somerset Local Education Authority. We have capacity for up to 105 pupils of school age on roll across four classes: our Early Years Class (Rowan) made up of our preschool Little Acorns and our reception children; Year 1&2 (Oak); Year 3&4 (Willow) and Year 5&6 (Chestnut) and also an inclusion class known as The Beehive, which supports a number of children from across the school. Our Little Acorns preschool became part of Rowan Class this year, with around 15 children accessing sessions during the week, up to 8 children at a time.
The school is situated on the edge of the village of Wookey, with beautiful views across to the Mendip Hills in an area of outstanding natural beauty, just under two miles from the Cathedral City of Wells. Wookey is a thriving village with a strong sense of community.
The school was founded in 1844 by St Matthew’s Church, Wookey. Alumni include HG Wells who, in 1880, joined the school as a pupil tutor for a short period, following his uncle who was head teacher at that time. The school has obviously seen many changes since the Victorian era and now possesses more modern accommodation but still maintains much of its original character.
The main school building consists of two large classrooms, a smaller staffroom, meeting and intervention room, a small dining hall/teaching space, a library and the rest of the former schoolhouse, which incorporates the administrative part of the school. There are three further classrooms next to the main school building, set in extensive grounds. We have a spacious playing field with a Forest School area, raised beds, adventurous play resources and fixed workout equipment - we are an OPAL school and these outdoor spaces are used throughout the year in all weathers. There are also two playgrounds with table tennis tables, a traverse wall, Harrison’s Hut for drama, music and calm play and an undercover play space.
Parents have a positive role to play in school, helping teachers and children in many areas such as reading, art and craft, cooking and gardening and during visits. The Wookey School Association (WSA) helps to raise funds for equipment and activities by organising many social events throughout the year.
In the latest Ofsted Report (January 2025) the school was judged as good for personal development and requiring improvement in all other areas. The inspectors acknowledged work staff had already done in making the necessary improvements and stated that time would be needed to see the results; the latest set of national testing outcomes evidenced the success we have had in this.

Clubs and Activities
Clubs, enrichment and activities available to children at Wookey Primary School.
Clubs offered
We run a variety of clubs throughout the school year. In recent times we have offered clubs for Lego, Dance, Cross Country, athletics, art, science, chess, multi-sports and Farm Club. Some are run by school staff, some by volunteers and others are externally provided. We seek to offer a range of options, including at least one free club every term.
We take a flexible approach to ensure that clubs are targeted towards different age groups, as we recognise how difficult it is to create a single programme suitable for all ages. Clubs are initially aimed at children in Year 1 and above, although Reception aged children are encouraged to take part in clubs in the second half of the year.
Holiday Activities
Active Camps run locally during the school holidays, delivered by TLE sports coaches. We advertise a range of activity options for families in our newsletter in the run-up to school holidays.
Wrap Around Care
We also offer wrap around care, run by our own staff. You can find out more on our Wrap Around Care page.

School Premiums and Funding
Information about pupil premium, sport premium and other school funding reports.
What is Pupil Premium?
Pupil Premium is an annual government grant provided to schools to support student development and academic success. Each school receives this additional funding based on specific criteria, including children who have qualified for free school meals at any point in the last six years. Financial support is also provided for children who are adopted, currently in local authority care, or from service families. While these funds benefit the entire school community through enhanced resources, they are primarily targeted to provide tailored academic and emotional support for eligible children. Ultimately, this funding ensures that every student receives the guidance needed to thrive socially, emotionally, and academically.
Eligibility is determined primarily through parental benefits that also entitle children to free school meals. However, if you receive certain benefits, the school can receive pupil premium funding as well. You must fill in all the details on the free school meal form for us to access this funding.
All pupils in YR-2 receive a free school meal under the universal infant free school meals policy (UIFSM).
You can find information below which gives details of our Pupil Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.
PE and Sports Premium
Schools receive a PE and Sports Premium based on the number of children on roll (ends December 2026). This is allocated to improve PE and sport provision in schools, including through active outdoor play and learning. Schools are required to report on how this money is spent and the impact of the spending. Details of how we have spent this money at Wookey Primary School can be found below. A new report is published every year, this year at the end of September.

Safeguarding
Safeguarding information and contacts for pupils, parents and carers.
At Wookey Primary School we are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, and we expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.
We have consistent, effective safeguarding procedures in place to support children, families and staff. All staff and governors receive appropriate training, guidance and support in child protection annually, as well as updates across the year.
We work in partnership with other agencies when there are concerns about a child’s welfare. We will normally discuss any concerns with parents and carers first, unless doing so might place the child at greater risk.
Our Safeguarding Team
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL): Mrs Davies
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL): Miss Furner
Reporting a Concern
Staff record concerns, including observations and conversations, and report them to a safeguarding lead the same day, without conducting their own investigations. Any concern that a member of staff may be unsuitable to work with children should be reported confidentially to a safeguarding lead.
If you have a safeguarding concern, please contact the school office and ask to speak to a safeguarding lead.

The Beehive
The Beehive: Nurture & Inclusive Provision at Wookey At Wookey Primary School, we are proud to be a fully inclusive setting. We believe that inclusion is not simply physical presence in a room, it is about a genuine sense of belonging. The Beehive is our small-group nurture setting designed to build safety, secure strong learning foundations, and ensure no child leaves Wookey without the skills to thrive.
How The Beehive Works
The Beehive follows Somerset’s Inclusive Curriculum Model, providing a time-limited, flexible intervention where the balance between whole-class and small-group learning is tailored to every child.
A Day in The Beehive
Watch This Space! - We are currently developing a Sensory Garden right next to our new Beehive building! Designed to be a calming, immersive outdoor space, it will be accessible to anyone across the whole school community who needs a quiet moment to regulate, explore, and recharge.
The 6-Step Journey in The Beehive While every child’s path through The Beehive is fluid and individualised, our strategic progression follows six supportive steps:
The Impact: In Our Community’s Words
What our children say:
“In class I used to feel like everyone was staring at me and I couldn’t do my work. I don’t feel like that now.”; “It is fun, I don’t think I would be at school without the Beehive.”; “It is a place where I can just be me.”
What our parents say:
“It has been life-changing; he feels safe and can actually access an education now.”; “The Beehive has brought out my child’s humour… they now smile without it being forced.”; “We no longer have battles to get into school; their worries and anxiety have reduced significantly.”
Transformative Whole-School Outcomes
Key Contacts & Outreach
If you are a parent with questions or a colleague from another school who would like to learn more about how The Beehive works, we would love to connect with you! Please reach out to our team via the school office: school.423@wookeyprimaryschool.co.uk

Little Acorns Preschool
Little Acorns Preschool
Little Acorns provides preschool places from 3 years old and is fully part of Wookey Primary School.
Little Acorns Preschool
At Wookey Primary School, we are proud to have our own preschool called Little Acorns, providing places from 3 years old, with our settling-in period tailored to meet each child’s individual needs. Originally an independently-managed playgroup, we have been inspiring the youngest members of our community to learn and grow for over 30 years.
This year, our Little Acorns preschoolers are joining our reception children in our newly-created Early Years Class. They will benefit from a purpose-made classroom and fabulous outdoor space. Teaching will be by the class teachers, Mrs Salma and Mrs Fisher and assisted by a specialist Early Years Practitioner, Miss Pronenko. Our Early Years team has a wealth of experience and are excited to be able to use the Wookey curriculum, values and ethos with the children from the very start of their learning journeys.
The children at Little Acorns will share playtimes and spaces, join in with weekly celebration assemblies and enjoy wider curriculum learning experiences with children and staff from across the school.
To arrange a visit, please contact us on 01749 673650 or School.423@wookeyprimaryschool.co.uk. To ask about available spaces, please email chloe.brice@wookeyprimaryschool.co.uk, or use Seesaw to message Mrs Salma if your child is already on roll.
Preschool Policies

Admissions
Information for families applying for a place at Wookey Primary School.
Starting School
If your child is due to start school you are advised to read the Somerset Primary Admissions Guide carefully before making your application. This includes everything you need to know in order to make your school place application. Applications are made through the online portal on the Somerset County Council website.
In Year Admissions
Somerset County Council is our Admissions Authority. We can process admissions to year groups that are under our Planned Admission Number (PAN) of 15, but if a year group is at or above PAN, applications have to be agreed by Somerset County Council.
If you would like to find out more about any aspect of admissions please see the Somerset Primary Admissions Guide.
Key Dates
Closing dates and outcome dates for school place applications are published each year by Somerset County Council. Please check the Primary Admissions Guide for the dates relevant to your application year.
Contact for Admissions
Admissions and Entitlements Team County Hall, Taunton, Somerset, TA1 4DY
Opening hours: Monday to Thursday 8:30am–5:00pm, Friday 8:30am–4:30pm.
You are also very welcome to contact the school office to arrange a visit or ask a question about admissions.
Email: schooladmissions@somerset.gov.uk
Phone: 0300 123 2224
